name: Chironex fleckeri
notes: Tentacles carry extremely potent venom that can cause cardiac arrest in minutes.

name: Carukia barnesi
notes: Tiny jellyfish whose venom causes Irukandji syndrome; stings can be life-threatening.

name: Synanceia verrucosa
notes: Dorsal spines inject venom causing extreme pain, tissue necrosis, and sometimes death.

name: Dasyatis pastinaca
notes: Tail spine can puncture deep into tissue, occasionally severing major blood vessels.

name: Androctonus australis
notes: Among the most dangerous scorpions; venom can cause respiratory failure.

name: Leiurus quinquestriatus
notes: Highly toxic venom that can be fatal, especially to small animals and children.

name: Acanthaster planci
notes: Long venomous spines cause deep wounds and can lead to serious systemic reactions.

name: Diadema setosum
notes: Needle-like spines break easily and can cause severe injury and infection.

name: Pterois volitans
notes: Fin spines deliver venom causing intense pain and systemic symptoms; invasive in some regions.

name: Lonomia obliqua
notes: Venomous spines induce severe clotting disorders and hemorrhage; many deaths recorded.

name: Phyllobates terribilis
notes: Skin secretes batrachotoxin; tiny amounts can stop the heart of large animals.

name: Hapalochlaena lunulata
notes: Delivers tetrodotoxin via bite, causing rapid paralysis and respiratory arrest.

name: Conus geographus
notes: Shoots a harpoon-like tooth with conotoxin; several human fatalities documented.

name: Tetraodontidae spp.
notes: Organs contain tetrodotoxin; ingestion can cause rapid paralysis and death.

name: Taricha granulosa
notes: Skin contains enough tetrodotoxin to kill large predators if ingested.

name: Oxyuranus microlepidotus
notes: One of the most venomous snakes; untreated bites are frequently fatal.

name: Ophiophagus hannah
notes: Preys on other snakes; large venom yield makes bites highly dangerous.

name: Dendroaspis polylepis
notes: Fast-moving snake with potent neurotoxic venom and high untreated fatality rate.

name: Atrax robustus
notes: Aggressive spider with neurotoxic venom; historically many serious envenomations.

name: Phoneutria nigriventer
notes: Highly mobile, potent venom; medically important and potentially lethal.

name: Hystrix cristata
notes: Long quills can deeply impale predators; infection and organ damage may be fatal.

name: Erethizon dorsatum
notes: Barbed quills are difficult to remove and can kill attacking animals via infection.

name: Carnegiea gigantea
notes: Large spines and heavy arms can impale or crush animals under certain conditions.

name: Cylindropuntia fulgida
notes: Barbed segments detach and embed deeply, causing painful wounds and infections.

name: Birgus latro
notes: Huge claws can crush bone and cause life-threatening injuries in smaller animals.

name: Odontodactylus scyllarus
notes: Raptorial appendages strike with bullet-like force, shattering shells and injuring prey.

name: Carcharodon carcharias
notes: Serrated teeth and powerful bite cause massive blood loss and rapid death in prey.

name: Crocodylus niloticus
notes: Ambushes at water edges; bite and death-roll behavior frequently lethal to large prey.

name: Hermodice carunculata
notes: Stinging bristles cause burning pain and tissue damage; large exposures may be serious.

name: Atropa belladonna
notes: Contains atropine and scopolamine; ingestion can cause respiratory failure and death.

name: Conium maculatum
notes: All parts are highly poisonous; small doses can kill humans and livestock via respiratory paralysis.

name: Cicuta maculata
notes: Often called the most deadly plant in North America; cicutoxin causes convulsions and rapid death if ingested.

name: Nerium oleander
notes: Cardiac glycosides in leaves and flowers can cause fatal heart arrhythmias.

name: Abrus precatorius
notes: Seeds contain abrin, one of the most potent plant toxins; a single chewed seed can be lethal.

name: Ricinus communis
notes: Seeds contain ricin, a powerful cytotoxin that can cause multi-organ failure and death.

name: Datura stramonium
notes: Rich in tropane alkaloids; overdose leads to delirium, hyperthermia, and potentially fatal heart problems.

name: Digitalis purpurea
notes: Cardiac glycosides can cause dangerous arrhythmias and cardiac arrest if ingested.

name: Urtica dioica
notes: Hollow hairs inject irritants, causing painful welts; not usually lethal but very defensive.

name: Acacia nilotica
notes: Long sharp thorns can seriously injure large herbivores and deter most browsers.

name: Yersinia pestis
notes: Agent of bubonic plague; untreated infection can kill over half of infected hosts.

name: Bacillus anthracis
notes: Forms durable spores; inhalational anthrax is highly lethal without rapid treatment.

name: Clostridium botulinum
notes: Produces botulinum toxin, one of the most potent known; causes flaccid paralysis and respiratory failure.

name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
notes: Leading infectious killer globally; untreated pulmonary TB has a high mortality rate.

name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (MDR)
notes: Multidrug-resistant strain causing severe, often deadly infections in hospitals.

name: Cryptococcus neoformans
notes: Soil and wood-inhabiting yeast causing cryptococcosis; high mortality in immunocompromised hosts.

name: Candida auris
notes: Multidrug-resistant yeast causing invasive infections with high mortality rates.

name: Aspergillus fumigatus
notes: Airborne spores can cause invasive aspergillosis; often lethal in immunocompromised patients.

name: Histoplasma capsulatum
notes: Soil fungus associated with bat and bird droppings; inhalation leads to histoplasmosis, sometimes fatal.

name: Dunkleosteus terrelli
notes: Armored fish with massive biting plates; capable of crushing armored prey.

name: Hyneria lindae
notes: Large predatory fish with powerful jaws; dangerous to most contemporaneous vertebrates.

name: Dimetrodon grandis
notes: Sail-backed predator with sharp teeth; top land carnivore of many Permian ecosystems.

name: Gorgonops torvus
notes: Saber-toothed predator with large canines; capable of killing large herbivores.

name: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
notes: Semi-aquatic theropod with powerful jaws and claws, preying on large fish and other animals.

name: Tyrannosaurus rex
notes: Massive carnivore with bone-crushing bite; apex predator of Late Cretaceous North America.

name: Ankylosaurus magniventris
notes: Heavily armored herbivore with tail club; blows could cripple or kill large predators.

name: Stegosaurus stenops
notes: Tail spikes capable of inflicting deep, lethal puncture wounds in predators.

name: Triceratops horridus
notes: Three facial horns and bony frill; charge could impale large predators.

name: Spicomellus afer
notes: Early armored dinosaur with unique spiked armor; heavily defended against predators.

name: Deinonychus antirrhopus
notes: Sickle-shaped toe claws designed for slashing; dangerous pack hunter.

name: Astrocaryum standleyanum
notes: Palm tree with sharp spines on trunk and fronds; causes deep puncture wounds and infections.
